# looot-mentions

> Open-source brand and keyword listening. Give it keywords and brand names. It searches Reddit, X, Hacker News, news, YouTube and the web through looot, removes duplicates, tags each mention by source, rule-based sentiment and intent (complaint, question, recommendation request, comparison), and writes a markdown digest of what is new since the last run.

## Run it
- Free check, no token: `npm run mentions -- --demo`
- Price a real run, no call made: `npm run mentions -- --keywords "Acme,Beta" --dry-run`
- Real run: `LOOOT_TOKEN=... npm run mentions -- --config mentions.yaml`
- Output: `digests/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (new mentions) and `data/mentions.json` (everything seen, plus spend per month)
- Daily: `.github/workflows/mentions.yml` runs it from cron and spends nothing until the LOOOT_TOKEN secret exists.

## Rules
- Always run `--dry-run` first and show the list-price cost to the user.
- The per-run cap (maxSpendPerRunUsd) and the monthly cap (monthlyCapUsd) are enforced before calls are sent.
- A source marked "still running at looot" is pending, not failed.
- Sentiment and intent come from word lists in config/rules.json. Each mention shows the words that produced its label.

## Files
- src/engine/engine.ts: plan, quote, run, dedupe
- src/engine/sources.ts: endpoint ids, inputs and parsers per source
- src/engine/rules.ts and config/rules.json: sentiment and intent rules
- skills/mentions/SKILL.md: Claude Code skill
